counterfactual_missing_items: No evidence of microangiopathic hemolysis (e.g., schistocytes) to support HUS
No elevated creatine kinase to support rhabdomyolysis
No interstitial nephritis pattern on biopsy (e.g., interstitial inflammation)
decisive_items: B) The content of these tubules shows strong reactivity for hemoglobin by immunohistochemistry (immunoperoxidase stain, 20× objective)
response.rationale: R4 uniquely combines low haptoglobin, elevated LDH, and hemoglobin-reactive tubules on biopsy, directly indicating hemolysis with hemoglobinuria and renal tubular injury. R3 captures the renal tubular damage and temporal drug association but omits the hemolysis markers, making it a plausible but less complete alternative. R1 lacks haptoglobin/LDH and biopsy hemoglobin evidence; R5 lacks renal biopsy and creatinine; R2 lacks hemolysis and biopsy specificity.

rejected.why: HUS requires microangiopathic hemolysis with schistocytes, not present; lacks haptoglobin/LDH and hemoglobin biopsy evidence.
Rhabdomyolysis would show elevated CK and not hemoglobinuria; lacks renal biopsy and creatinine evidence.
Acute interstitial nephritis is not supported by biopsy showing tubular hemoglobin casts; lacks hemolysis markers.
